newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan shares down in Tokyo on estimated loss.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan shares down in Tokyo on estimated loss.

text.p: Shares of Yaohan Japan Corp fell sharply in early Tokyo on Thursday on the company's recent announcement that it would post a net parent loss for the last business year.
As of 0100 GMT, the shares were down 17 yen at 304 yen, making the firm the third biggest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Turnover was 448,000.

Yaohan said on Wednesday that it had revised down its earnings estimate for the 1996/97 business year. It forecast a parent net loss of 35.92 billion yen, compared with its earlier estimate of a 930 million yen profit. Yaohan posted a net profit of 453 million yen the year before.
Yaohan said it would post a loss because it had earmarked reserves for losses from loans to its subsidiaries.
Yaohan will announce its earnings for 1996/97 on Friday.

In February, Yaohan, the flagship firm of an international retailing group, announced a restructuring programme including a reduction of group debt subject to interest payments to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen in the next two years.
